key_insight: QCNO maps inhomogeneous neutrino fast flavor transformation onto TEBD2 quantum circuits, enabling a single framework for exact dynamics, backend execution, and fault-tolerant resource estimates.
engineering_relevance: The work gives a concrete path to assess whether quantum hardware can eventually simulate strongly correlated neutrino flavor evolution, while quantifying the circuit depth and error budgets needed for near- and long-term devices.
method: Map the forward-scattering neutrino Hamiltonian with advection and finite-range interactions to TEBD2 product-formula circuits.
Benchmark ideal evolution against exact many-body dynamics for the transverse fast flavor instability.
Estimate NISQ performance and fault-tolerant T-gate costs up to N=50 using the restricted interaction graph.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of exact many-body evolution through N=30, noisy-backend polarization RMSEs around 0.1-0.3, TEBD2 error near 10^-3, and about 1.4×10^4 T gates per qubit for open boundaries.
watch_item: The resource estimates depend on the specific interaction graph and synthesis tolerance, so hardware noise and fault-tolerant overheads may shift the feasibility window significantly.
paper_title: Quantum Co-Design of Inhomogeneous Many-Body Neutrino Fast Flavor Transformation
